title: Shared wire vocabulary
description: Every name a WattSteer response uses more than once, defined exactly once. `docs/domain-model.md` is the naming authority; `docs/specs/api-surface.md` fixes the casing (snake_case on the wire) and the nine vocabulary rules these definitions exist to make structural. A grep for `common.schema.json#/$defs/band` finds every band on the surface, which is rule 1.

cut_category.description: One rung of NT DOP 0022 §5.1.2's ordem de corte: hydro that can be held back without spilling, thermal outside merit order, hydro that can only be held back by spilling, and renewables. A rule about ONS's dispatch decision, which WattSteer does not take - it is here so a plan can say which rung it acts on.

subsystem.title: Subsystem
subsystem.description: An enum with exactly four members. `SIN` is ONS's national aggregate row, filtered at the ingest boundary, and is deliberately NOT a member: a national figure lives under a `national` key with its derivation named (vocabulary rule 6).

technology.title: Technology
technology.description: The two variable renewable fleets. Uppercase, case-sensitively, everywhere a value is serialized including the `technology=` query parameter. `wind_mwh` is a snake_case *field name* under the wire's casing rule and is not a spelling of the value.

band.title: Band
band.description: A P10/P50/P90 triple - the shape of every quantity the forecaster emits. Quantiles do not add: two bands are never summed componentwise. Referenced rather than inlined everywhere it appears (vocabulary rule 1), and closed to additional properties so an expectation cannot be smuggled inside one (vocabulary rule 2).

technology_split.title: TechnologySplit
technology_split.description: Two scalars, and nothing else (vocabulary rule 3). The forecaster publishes no per-technology band, so an object carrying a `p10` under the split must fail validation rather than reach a chart that would draw it.

vintage_fidelity.title: VintageFidelity
vintage_fidelity.description: Stamped on every object carrying a metric or a historical number (vocabulary rule 9), and never averaged across values by anything.

threshold_mw.title: ThresholdMw
threshold_mw.description: The parameter that produced the numbers beside it, carried on every object it applies to (vocabulary rule 8). Defaults: 5 MW at subsystem grain, 1 MW at reporting-entity grain.

max_gap_hours.title: MaxGapHours
max_gap_hours.description: How many sub-threshold hours an episode may contain. Default 0: one hour below the threshold ends the episode.

utc_instant.title: UtcInstant
utc_instant.description: ISO-8601 with an explicit `Z`. There is no offset-carrying local timestamp anywhere on this surface; the two representations are UTC instants and Brasilia civil dates, and mixing them is what the domain model's interval convention exists to prevent.

civil_date.title: CivilDate
civil_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, a civil date in `America/Sao_Paulo`. Never an instant.

clock_time.title: ClockTime
clock_time.description: `HH:MM` in `America/Sao_Paulo`; minutes are always `00`. `24:00` is the exclusive end of the day.

gate_profile.title: GateProfile
gate_profile.description: Which of the two daily gates published this. `gate_early` is D-1 09:00 BRT on the 00Z weather run; `gate_late` is D-1 19:00 BRT on the 12Z run.

origin_kind.title: OriginKind
origin_kind.description: `served` is a record of a publication. `backfilled_holdout` is a counterfactual publication instant and is never returned by a live forecast route under any query.

producer.title: ForecastProducer
producer.description: Identity, never copy. The producer of a *curtailment* forecast is `wattsteer`; `open_meteo` is the producer of the weather run it consumed, which is a different fact about a different artifact.

forecast_origin.title: ForecastOrigin
forecast_origin.description: The identity of the run that produced a forecast. Every surface that shows a forecast must name it. `weather_run_label` rides beside the WattSteer origin rather than making a screen choose which of the two facts to call "the run".

run_label.description: For a `wattsteer` forecast, the artifact version.

published_at.description: `gate_at(target_date, gate_profile)` - a property of the target date, not of the request.

age_hours.description: Derived and returned, so no screen computes a date difference against a clock it may not have.

weather_run_label.description: The weather run the forecast was built on, e.g. "D-1 12Z".

risk_class.title: RiskClass
risk_class.description: A code; the client translates it.

risk_bins.title: RiskBins
risk_bins.description: The cut points the risk class was read off, published beside every risk class so the class is checkable rather than asserted.

avoidability.title: Avoidability
avoidability.description: `avoided / baseline`. **`null`, never 0, when baseline curtailment is zero** (vocabulary rule 4): the ratio is undefined, and a zero would read as "nothing could be avoided" rather than "there was nothing to avoid". The null is meaningful and the schema admits it explicitly.

reason_code.title: ReasonCode
reason_code.description: ONS's restriction reason, verbatim from the dictionary. The identifier travels and the English gloss does not (vocabulary rule 7); the gloss is a `t()` key. `REL` is grid unavailability, not "relaxamento".

restriction_origin.title: RestrictionOrigin
restriction_origin.description: Whether a restriction was local to the entity or systemic.

unit_code.title: UnitCode
unit_code.description: A unit as a code, so a reading is formatted in the reader's locale rather than the server's.

band_unavailable_reason.title: BandUnavailableReason
band_unavailable_reason.description: Why a published figure has no band - an identity, never a sentence. One member today: a quantile of a sum needs a joint draw, and the path ensemble is drawn per subsystem.

scenario_hash.title: ScenarioHash
scenario_hash.description: `sha256:` followed by the digest of the canonical scenario bytes.

solver.title: SolverReceipt
solver.description: What actually solved it. Carried so a plan is attributable to a backend and a build.

economic_scenario.title: EconomicScenario
economic_scenario.description: Money appears only as a labelled scenario with its assumed rate visible. Never a market price.

scored_realisation.title: ScoredRealisation
scored_realisation.description: The four scalars evaluated on one realisation of the forecast.

dispatch_hour.title: DispatchHour
dispatch_hour.description: One hour of the plan, in `America/Sao_Paulo` local hours.

episode.title: CurtailmentEpisode
episode.description: A read-time view, never a stored table. Every episode carries the `threshold_mw` and `max_gap_hours` that produced it (vocabulary rule 8), because an unstamped duration cannot be compared with another one.

ended_at.description: Exclusive: the valid_time of the first hour below threshold.
